subject.title: Telegram: allow native channel commands in explicitly allowed chats

question: Should Telegram channel_post native/plugin commands be allowed on explicit chat entry alone, or must sender_chat allowlists and channel-aware callback/session routing be defined before this command surface lands?
rationale: The code change expands a Telegram command execution surface on a senderless update type, and the safe policy cannot be inferred from tests alone while the paired policy issue remains open.

options.title: Require Auth And Callback Semantics First
options.body: Keep the PR open but require explicit channel authorization, sender_chat-aware allowlist behavior, channel-aware callback/session routing, and redacted live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Fold Into The Policy Issue
options.body: Pause this branch and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49062 to choose channel_post sender-policy semantics before code moves forward.

options.title: Accept Explicit-Chat-Only Semantics
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept explicit-chat-only channel_post commands, but that needs visible security review, docs, tests, and live proof first.

recommendation.title: Require Auth And Callback Semantics First
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but require explicit channel authorization, sender_chat-aware allowlist behavior, channel-aware callback/session routing, and redacted live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this owner most closely to Telegram native command and callback behavior that must be decided together.
